proposal.hypothesis: With the existing 128-thread blocks and unchanged one-element-per-thread mapping, reduce0 performs seven CTA-wide barriers in its shared-memory tree. Reducing each warp with the existing sync-intrinsic helper, writing one partial per warp, then using one CTA barrier and a warp-0 reduction may reduce synchronization overhead. The tail remains zero-padded and every launched lane participates. The baseline is correct at a mean 47.08 µs; no candidate speedup or correctness is claimed before controller evaluation.

retained: Retain the same global load mapping and zero-pad out-of-range tail elements, but keep each loaded value in a register for the warp reduction.
Use the existing warpReduceSum helper with __activemask() for each warp; on the supplied SM 8.0+ target the int specialization uses __reduce_add_sync.
Have lane 0 of each warp write its partial sum to shared memory; use one __syncthreads() before warp 0 reduces the partials and writes the block result.
Leave run's 128-thread launch, reduction pass loop, scratch selection, and output copy unchanged.
